item.title: Saudi Arabia executes five Ethiopians for hashish smuggling
item.description: Saudi Arabia has executed five Ethiopian nationals convicted of drug smuggling, bringing the kingdom’s execution toll this year to 205, according to the country’s Interior Ministry. The five were convicted of participating in smuggling hashish into the kingdom, the ministry said in a statement published by the official Saudi Press Agency on Thursday. They were executed in Asir, a province in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The latest executions are the third such announcement involving Ethiopian nationals in recent months. Five Ethiopians were executed on the same day in June, while another five were put to death in July. With the latest executions, 32 Ethiopian nationals have been executed in Saudi Arabia this year, making them the largest foreign national group among those executed. Human Rights Watch warned in July that at least 79 Ethiopians faced an imminent risk of execution over similar drug-related charges. Saudi Arabia recorded 356 executions last year, the highest annual figure in the kingdom’s history. Thousands of Ethiopians work in low-skilled jobs in Saudi Arabia, with many travelling to the oil-rich kingdom through the perilous Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa via Yemen. item.title: Atiku flags off ADC campaign in Kebbi, pledges security, fuel subsidy restoration
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi BIRNIN KEBBI — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to address Nigeria’s security challenges and restore fuel subsidy if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the promises during the flag-off of his campaign in Kebbi State, where he described the forthcoming election as a referendum on the policies of the President Bola Tinubu administration. He said the election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to decide whether to retain the current government or embrace an alternative amid concerns over economic hardship and insecurity. Supporters of the ADC converged on the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the campaign rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party members for attending the gathering despite what he described as intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 election would be a referendum on the performance of the Tinubu administration, adding that hunger, insecurity and unemployment would feature prominently in the campaign. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that could not be stopped by intimidation. He urged Kebbi residents to vote for Abubakar Malami as governor, Atiku as president and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections. Atiku and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the Tinubu administration, alleging that they were legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. They described the ADC as an alternative for Nigerians seeking improved security and a reversal of the fuel subsidy policy. The rally climaxed with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as its governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Meanwhile, security was heightened in Birnin Kebbi ahead of Atiku’s arrival, with security personnel deployed across parts of the state capital to prevent any breakdown of law and order. The campaign rally ended peacefully, with no reported attacks or destruction of vehicles, unlike the violence alleged to have accompanied the party’s campaign activities in Sokoto State. item.title: Two killed, 20 abducted in Kaduna community attack
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — Two persons have reportedly been killed and 20 others abducted after suspected terrorists invaded Akwando community in Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The attackers reportedly stormed the community around noon on Wednesday, shooting residents and abducting several people. The police had yet to officially confirm the incident as of Thursday. The President of the Kuturmi Unity Development Association (KUDA), Dr Joseph Ariko, and its Publicity Secretary, Manasseh Samuel Akwando, disclosed the attack in a statement expressing concern over the security situation in Kuturmi communities. The association said the latest attack had worsened the plight of residents still struggling to recover from previous assaults, particularly the Easter Sunday attack on Ariko community. It described the recurring incidents as a threat to the lives, livelihoods and ancestral heritage of the affected communities. KUDA identified the 20 persons reportedly abducted from Akwando as Usman Galadima, La’a’zarus Genesis, Madalin Markus, Happy Stephen, Lovet Ishaya, Afiniki Irimeya, Amina Ahmadu, Miracle Genesis, Hellen Irimeya and Musa Genesis. Others are Janet Irimeya, Gloria Markus, Zila Stephen, Alis Ahmadu, Haske Ahmadu, Great Isiac, Hanatu Irimeya, Desmon Ishaya, Siam Shagari and Nansy Genesis. The association recalled that the Easter Sunday attack on Ariko reportedly claimed five lives at the scene, while another 17 victims subsequently died in captivity. It also cited an earlier attack on Awon community, during which two persons were reportedly killed and 11 others abducted. According to KUDA, five of those abducted in Awon regained their freedom on November 3, 2026, but one reportedly died the following day. Another victim escaped, while five others allegedly died in captivity. The association said the recurring attacks had forced residents to flee their homes, abandon their farmlands and suspend economic activities for fear of further assaults. It further alleged that armed groups had restricted residents’ access to their ancestral lands, compelling some to pay levies before cultivating their farms or harvesting agricultural produce. However, KUDA said the allegations required independent investigation and urged security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents and identify those responsible. It called on the Federal and Kaduna State governments, as well as the Kachia Local Government Council, to strengthen security in Akwando, Ariko, Awon and other vulnerable communities. Specifically, the association demanded the deployment of adequately equipped security personnel, establishment of permanent security posts, regular patrols and effective early-warning mechanisms to prevent further attacks. It also appealed for coordinated security operations to secure the release of the 20 residents reportedly abducted in Akwando and others still being held captive. item.title: Power generation drops to 3,659MW as FG explains supply disruptions
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Electricity generation on Nigeria’s national grid dropped to 3,659 megawatts (MW) as of 3pm on Thursday, from a peak of 3,996MW recorded on Wednesday, amid worsening power supply across parts of the country. The Federal Government attributed the decline to gas supply constraints to thermal power plants, reduced water inflows into hydroelectric reservoirs and operational challenges within the power sector. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that the decline had affected electricity allocation to Distribution Companies (DisCos), resulting in shorter hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. Data on the distribution load allocation dashboard as of 5:39pm on Thursday showed that the 11 electricity distribution companies received a combined allocation of 3,031MW. Abuja Disco received the highest allocation of 669MW, followed by Ibadan Disco with 413MW and Port Harcourt Disco with 338MW. Benin Disco received 279MW, Enugu 267MW, Eko 256MW, Ikeja 249MW, Kano 173MW, Kaduna 167MW, Jos 146MW, while Yola Disco received the lowest allocation of 74MW. The Federal Ministry of Power, in a statement on Thursday by the Special Adviser (Media and Publicity) to the Minister of Power, Adeola Adelabu, acknowledged complaints by electricity consumers in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo states over worsening supply in recent days. The Ministry noted that the affected areas had recently experienced noticeable improvements in electricity supply before the latest disruptions. It, however, ruled out a major or systemic failure of the national grid, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges in parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation. Acknowledging the impact of the disruptions on consumers, the Ministry said: “We recognise what every hour without power means for individuals, families and businesses, and we do not take it lightly.” It added that the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, was working with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), NISO and electricity distribution companies to address the challenges and restore normal supply. According to the Ministry, the Minister had engaged relevant operators to resolve the operational constraints, accelerate ongoing maintenance and keep the public informed about restoration efforts. In a separate statement, NISO confirmed that limited gas availability had constrained the ability of affected thermal generating stations to operate at their available capacities, while reduced water inflows had affected hydroelectric generation. item.title: SDP condemns attempts to disqualify ADC presidential candidate, Atiku
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Social Democratic Party (SDP) has condemned alleged attempts to disqualify the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, insisting that political parties should be allowed to freely present candidates for the 2027 general elections. The party also called on the judiciary, security agencies and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remain impartial and protect the country’s democratic process. The SDP National Chairman, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, stated this on Thursday in Abuja while addressing journalists after a meeting with the party’s nine governorship candidates from different states. Gombe, who said the SDP would not participate in the proposed ‘Rainbow Coalition’, reaffirmed the party’s commitment to contesting the 2027 elections under its own political platform. He also accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of allegedly plotting to infiltrate opposition parties and weaken their ranks ahead of the elections. The SDP chairman alleged that the APC, having lost the confidence of Nigerians over its governance record, was using the proposed coalition to woo opposition members and undermine their unity. He, however, said the SDP was working with other opposition parties towards building a coalition of Nigerians committed to credible elections, including joint training of party agents and the establishment of common situation rooms to protect votes at polling units. Gombe reaffirmed the party’s commitment to presenting what he described as credible alternatives to Nigerians, particularly its presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and vice-presidential candidate, Prof. Usman Bugaje. He said: “I want to assure you that SDP, as a political party, has nothing to do with anything called Rainbow Coalition. “We are with other political parties in the opposition, doing everything possible to rescue our dear country through a coalition of the Nigerian people. “We are not into any Rainbow Coalition where we will have candidates here and profess support for the APC presidency. We are SDP and we are for SDP candidates.” He said the party had resolved to discipline any member who participated in the proposed arrangement without its authorisation. According to Gombe, the meeting with the governorship candidates was part of preparations to strengthen the party’s electoral strategies and improve its chances in the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027: Presidency seeks global safeguards against AI-generated falsehoods
item.description: –As Onanuga warns of threat to democratic institutions, public trust By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–THE Presidency has called for urgent global action to check the growing misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in political communication, warning that unchecked deployment of the technology could undermine democratic institutions, distort electoral processes and erode public trust ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Mr Bayo Onanuga, made the call on Thursday in Beijing, China, while delivering a paper titled, “AI and the Future of Global Communication”, at the 7th World Media Summit organised by Xinhua News Agency and the People’s Government of Beijing Municipality. Onanuga said the proliferation of AI-generated videos, images and other digital content for political purposes had made it imperative for governments, media organisations and technology stakeholders to establish safeguards against disinformation and manipulation. According to him, social media platforms, including X, Facebook and TikTok, were increasingly inundated with AI-generated content designed to advance political interests, entertain audiences and influence public opinion. With political activities and campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections gathering momentum, the presidential aide said AI had become a powerful instrument in the hands of politicians and their supporters, with the potential to serve both legitimate and destructive purposes. “We are in the thick of the political season and campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections, where new political leaders at the national and sub-national levels will be elected. AI, for good and bad, has become a powerful tool for electoral contests for politicians and their supporters. “Some political actors use AI to spread falsehoods, some use it satirically for entertainment, and some highlight candidates’ achievements,” he said. He stressed that the growing influence of AI in political communication demanded greater responsibility from political actors, media organisations and the general public, particularly in verifying information before creating, publishing or sharing digital content. While acknowledging the dangers associated with the technology, Onanuga cautioned against disregarding its enormous contributions to human development, particularly in medicine, mathematics and other areas of scientific innovation. He noted that AI had become deeply embedded in everyday life, citing its applications in vehicle safety systems, navigation and other technological solutions that had improved human efficiency and convenience. “Today, AI governs our existence, and we encounter it all the time. In the car, it warns you about your immediate surroundings. It maps your fastest route to your destination. item.title: ADC: Sokoto turnout prompted judgment voiding Atiku’s candidacy
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has alleged that the turnout at its political event in Sokoto influenced the timing of a court judgment that nullified the leadership of its David Mark-led faction and voided the party’s presidential candidacy. The party’s spokesperson, Bolaji Abdullahi, made the allegation on Channels Television’s Lunchtime Politics , while reacting to the judgment. Abdullahi said the party would challenge the ruling, insisting that the legal battle was part of what he described as sustained efforts to frustrate its political activities. He claimed that the ruling party was determined to remain in power and prevent Nigerians from having a democratic choice in the 2027 elections. “We’ve spent more time in the courts than we’ve spent on the campaign grounds, thanks to the ruling party,” he said. The ADC spokesperson alleged that the judgment was expedited following the party’s political outing in Sokoto. “But I think in the matter of hours after seeing what happened in Sokoto yesterday, the kind of reaction, the kind of turnout in Sokoto yesterday, they had to quickly go and dust up this and hurry up the judgment this morning,” Abdullahi said. He, however, said the ADC remained confident in its ability to challenge the ruling through the judicial process. “We will approach the same court. We believe in the judicial institution, regardless of the recklessness of some judges who have allowed themselves to be used as a tool for subverting democracy in Nigeria,” he said. Abdullahi said the party would apply for a stay of execution and appeal the judgment. He warned that if the ruling stood, the ADC could be prevented from fielding candidates for the presidential, governorship, National Assembly and other elections. “What is endangered is not the African Democratic Congress. What is endangered is Nigeria as a country and our democracy as we’ve known it,” he said. The ADC spokesperson maintained that the party’s message of change, affordability and improved living conditions had gained nationwide support, urging that Nigerians be allowed to choose their preferred leaders. He insisted that the judgment would not stand, adding that the party would continue its legal challenge. item.title: South Africans now leading drug trafficking cartels in Nigeria — NDLEA
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has raised the alarm over the growing involvement of South African nationals in drug trafficking networks operating in Nigeria, alleging that some are facilitating the movement of illicit substances through the country to other parts of the world. The agency said three South African nationals had been arrested in recent weeks with large consignments of heroin, cocaine and synthetic cannabis, popularly known as Loud. The Assistant Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Francis Okogun, disclosed this on Thursday during a joint media briefing by defence, security and intelligence agencies at the Office of the National Security Adviser in Abuja. Okogun said the arrests were significant because of the quantities of illicit drugs recovered and the potential implications for Nigeria’s international reputation. He said: “On the arrest of South African nationals in connection with drug trafficking, it is important to clarify that the issue has attracted attention because of the negative impression it could create about Nigeria internationally. “Our findings indicate that some foreign nationals are increasingly becoming involved in facilitating the movement of illicit drugs through Nigeria to other parts of the world. Some are also involved in bringing such substances into the country. “For the period under review, three individuals were arrested. What makes these arrests particularly significant is the large quantities of drugs recovered, including heroin, cocaine and synthetic cannabis, popularly known as Loud.” He said the agency was conducting investigations to establish the intended destinations of the seized drugs and identify the networks behind the consignments. “As you know, drug traffickers rarely volunteer information about their sponsors or the final destinations of their consignments. “We are therefore conducting painstaking investigations to establish the actual destinations of the drugs and identify the cartels responsible for the shipments,” he said. One of the recent arrests involved a 38-year-old South African woman, identified as Ms Will Jessica Ann, who was apprehended by NDLEA operatives at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after 5.75 kilogrammes of heroin were allegedly discovered in her luggage. The agency said the suspect concealed the drugs in 14 large blocks and allegedly used her three-year-old son as a cover to evade thorough security screening. She was arrested during the inward clearance of passengers aboard Qatar Airways flight QR 1433 from Doha to Abuja. According to the NDLEA, the suspect initially denied travelling with checked-in luggage but later admitted ownership of two bags after operatives established that their tags matched the claim tags attached to her passport. item.title: DHQ denies ceasefire with Boko Haram, ISWAP, others
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Defence Headquarters has dismissed reports alleging that the Federal Government or the Nigerian military entered into a ceasefire agreement with Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) or any other terrorist group. The military said its sustained and intensified offensives against terrorists, armed bandits, kidnappers and other criminal groups demonstrated that no such agreement existed. In one of the reports, a media platform had claimed that the Federal Government entered into a secret ceasefire agreement with the Boko Haram faction led by Bakura Doro, which allegedly contributed to relative calm in parts of the North-East for about three months. The report, citing three individuals said to have contacts among senior Boko Haram members, claimed that the ceasefire had been in effect since June and was expected to be extended. However, the Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba, dismissed the allegation, saying ongoing military operations and the successes recorded against armed groups showed that troops were not relenting. “I want to make it clear that there is nothing like a ceasefire anywhere, with Boko Haram, ISWAP or any terrorist group. “Considering the terrorists neutralised, suspects arrested, victims rescued and other successes recorded across our operations, it is clear that we are not relenting. We will continue to sustain pressure on these criminal elements. “Our operations are not limited to Boko Haram or ISWAP. They also target kidnappers and other criminal elements who take up arms against innocent citizens,” he said. Uba warned that individuals involved in criminal activities threatening the lives and security of Nigerians would either be neutralised through lawful military operations or brought to justice. “Anyone involved in criminal activities that threaten the lives and security of Nigerians will either be eliminated through lawful military operations or brought to justice,” he said. On reports of terrorists and bandits moving into parts of the country where they were previously less active, the defence spokesman described the development as evidence of the impact of ongoing military operations but said the Armed Forces were not taking the situation lightly. “The fact that some of them are leaving their former locations is a testimony to the successes of our operations. However, I assure you that we are not taking the situation lightly,” he said. He explained that the military was mapping locations where the fleeing armed groups might have relocated and taking proactive measures to prevent them from establishing new footholds. Uba said recent adjustments to the Armed Forces’ order of battle, including the establishment of new formations, battalions and units, were aimed at closing security gaps and strengthening military presence in vulnerable areas. item.title: I wait for trouble every morning at work, drop problems after work — Dangote
item.description: By Ebunoluwa Sessou Africa’s richest industrialist, Aliko Dangote, has said he confronts business challenges as they arise but deliberately leaves work-related problems behind when returning home to maintain a balance between his professional and personal life. Dangote spoke while delivering the keynote address at the 25th anniversary celebration of Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ), where he urged women entrepreneurs to dream bigger, remain focused and develop the resilience to overcome business challenges. Sharing his approach to managing pressure, the business mogul said he starts each working day prepared to confront unexpected difficulties but makes a conscious effort not to carry them home. “Every morning, when I get to my office, I’m waiting for trouble to come. When it comes, I face it. When I finish in the evening, as soon as I get to my gate, I drop all my problems and enter my house,” he said. Speaking on the theme, ‘Rooted, Rising and Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World’, Dangote challenged women to raise their ambitions and pursue opportunities beyond their present achievements. “I’m challenging you to actually increase your ambition. You can get there. Dream big, do not dream small,” he said. He acknowledged that doing business in Nigeria came with significant challenges, including infrastructure deficits, high operating costs and difficulties accessing affordable long-term financing. He, however, urged entrepreneurs not to allow such obstacles to discourage them, stressing that success required determination, proper planning and the willingness to confront difficult situations. “There is nothing in life that is good that will come easy. If it is easy, everybody will be the same. You must say, yes, it’s difficult, but I can surmount all these challenges and I can do it,” he said. Reflecting on his business journey, Dangote recalled the financial difficulties encountered during the construction of the Obajana cement plant, particularly the high interest rates charged by banks at the time. He said the financing challenges put pressure on the company’s operations and expansion plans but did not deter it from pursuing its long-term vision. The industrialist also emphasised the importance of maintaining good health while managing business responsibilities, disclosing that he regularly monitors his blood pressure and adjusts his schedule when necessary. He urged entrepreneurs to learn how to manage pressure and avoid allowing business challenges to overwhelm their personal lives. Dangote attributed business success to vision, tenacity, focus and the ability to confront challenges without being overwhelmed by emotions. He also disclosed that the Dangote Group was expanding its operations beyond Nigeria, announcing plans to establish a $2.5 million caprolactam farm and production line in Namibia. item.title: Troops kill three suspected kidnappers, recover four rifles in Kogi
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja Troops of the Nigerian Army, in collaboration with the Kogi State Vigilance Service (KSVS), have killed three suspected kidnappers and recovered four AK-47 rifles and a cache of ammunition during an operation in Igalamela/Odolu Local Government Area of Kogi State. The operation, conducted on November 4, followed earlier raids on suspected kidnappers’ hideouts in Edimogbo Forest, as security operatives extended their search towards the Obele Forest area in pursuit of fleeing suspects. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lieutenant Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement, saying the suspects attempted to escape on sighting the advancing troops, leading to an exchange of fire in which three of them were killed. Items recovered during the operation included four AK-47 rifles, 12 magazines, 336 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three bandoliers and an identity card. The statement said the operation was part of sustained efforts by troops of the 12 Composite Brigade, under the newly established 5 Division of the Nigerian Army, to dismantle kidnapping networks and deny criminal elements safe havens in Kogi State. It added that continued offensive operations, intelligence-driven patrols and searches of identified criminal hideouts were aimed at restricting the movement of kidnappers and restoring confidence among residents of affected communities. The Commander, 12 Composite Brigade, Brigadier General Kasim Umar Sidi, commended the troops and personnel of the Kogi State Vigilance Service for their resilience, professionalism and effectiveness during the operation. He urged them to sustain the momentum and ensure that criminal elements were denied freedom of action within the Brigade’s area of responsibility. The Army also appealed to residents of Kogi State and neighbouring communities to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations. item.title: Tinubu Congratulates Flamingos, Backs Team To Win U-17 World Cup
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their 3-1 victory over Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. In a statement issued by his media aide, Bayo Onanuga, the President described the team’s qualification for the final as a remarkable achievement that has brought immense pride and joy to millions of Nigerians at home and abroad. Tinubu also commended the coaching crew and everyone whose hard work and support contributed to the team’s successful campaign. As the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in the final, the President urged the players to remain focused, confident and determined, assuring them of the prayers, goodwill and unwavering support of Nigerians. “I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title. “I call on all Nigerians to rally behind the young ambassadors of the nation, whose achievements continue to showcase Nigeria’s sporting excellence and inspire a new generation of girls to pursue their dreams uninhibited. “Once again, Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added. President Bola Tinubu The Flamingos reached the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup for the first time after defeating Brazil 3-1 in their semi-final encounter in Morocco. The Nigerian girls produced a spirited second-half performance, scoring three goals before Brazil grabbed a late consolation. Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute, finishing off an assist from Oluwakemi Adegubyi to give Nigeria the lead. The Flamingos doubled their advantage in the 71st minute when Awawu Bashiru found the net, with Joseph providing the assist. Bashiru struck again in the 80th minute to make it 3-0, converting a pass from Oluebube Umejiaku as Nigeria took firm control of the encounter. Brazil pulled one back in the 89th minute through Greise Kelly, assisted by Yasmin Queiroz, but the goal came too late to prevent Nigeria from securing victory and a place in the final. item.title: 2027: Makinde rejects ‘turn-by-turn’ presidency, vows APM victory
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has vowed to win the 2027 election, urging Nigerians to reject what he described as ‘turn-by-turn nepotism’ in choosing the country’s president. Makinde spoke at the party’s South-West town hall meeting, where he argued that the region should not be expected to support President Bola Tinubu solely because he hails from the area. Citing the 1999 presidential election, he said the South-West had presented Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae as competing candidates, allowing Nigerians to choose their preferred leader. “As a matter of fact, what the South-West did was to present two of its finest candidates, two of its best, for Nigerians to choose from. Is there anything wrong with doing that this time around?” he asked. Makinde warned that treating the presidency as a regional entitlement could encourage sectional policies at the expense of national development. “We do not want turn-by-turn nepotism. We also do not want a situation where someone says, ‘I will execute projects in my zone because it is my turn,’” he said. The Oyo governor also accused the Federal Government of frustrating opposition parties, warning that democracy could not thrive under a political system that stifled competition. “There is no democracy in a one-party system,” he declared. On the economy, Makinde advocated a shift from dependence on federal allocations to productive economic activities that would create wealth and expand government revenue. “When they are productive, they become prosperous. When they become prosperous, tax their prosperity. Do not tax poverty,” he said. APM National Leader and Bauchi State Governor, Senator Bala Mohammed, described Makinde as a tested politician whose record in Oyo State informed the party’s decision to present him as its presidential candidate. “He understands Nigeria’s problems, particularly in infrastructure and public services. He has demonstrated his capacity to deliver by reducing infrastructure gaps at the sub-national level,” Mohammed said. The party’s vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, described the South-West meeting as encouraging, claiming the turnout indicated growing support for Makinde. National Chairman Yusuf Dantalle criticised insecurity, rising petroleum prices and what he described as the erosion of electoral accountability. “We must reset Nigeria. This is not democracy. item.title: Putin slams ‘political’ moves to keep Russia out of sport events
item.description: Vladimir Putin on Thursday slammed countries who oppose reinstating Russia into international sports as several European teams said they will refuse to play them at next year’s world ice hockey championships over the Ukraine war. Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Czech Republic on Tuesday all followed Finland in saying they would not play Russia at the 2027 world championships to be held in Germany. Russia has been banned from International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) events since Putin launched the 2022 war in Ukraine, but the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favour of admitting them to the world championships. Russia has been mostly banned from international sport since 2022 but some restrictions have eased in recent months — a trend slammed by Ukraine. Putin praised the International Olympic Committee and CAS for “taking decisions to uphold the Olympic Charter and its principles”, as restrictions have been eased. “Unfortunately, however, not all countries are prepared to honour the commitments they once undertook, and restrictions on Russian sport — which are political rather than legal — continue,” Putin told a televised government meeting. Amid the ice hockey stand-off, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday Russia would not be allowed to compete at next month’s World Junior Hockey Championships. The world championships are due to be held in Germany next May, but the draw and scheduling for the tournament have already taken place, without Russia. Putin has regularly appeared playing ice hockey during his long presidency. Russia’s war against Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, forced millions to displace and is Europe’s worst conflict since World War II. item.title: 2027: Police assure corps members, ad hoc staff of protection
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has assured members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and other ad hoc staff to be engaged by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of adequate protection during the 2027 general elections. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, gave the assurance at a joint media briefing of the Forum of Security and Intelligence Agencies, organised by the Office of the National Security Adviser. He was responding to concerns over reported abductions of corps members in different parts of the country, particularly as they are expected to form a significant part of INEC’s ad hoc workforce during the elections. Iniedu said the police had conducted an extensive threat assessment and were strengthening security arrangements to protect electoral personnel and materials and ensure the smooth conduct of the polls. He said the arrangements would be implemented in collaboration with other security agencies before, during and after the elections. “In every election cycle, there are potential threats to soft targets. However, as other targets become increasingly fortified by security agencies, criminals may attempt to exploit perceived vulnerabilities elsewhere. “The Nigeria Police Force has conducted an extensive threat assessment ahead of the forthcoming general elections, and we are adequately preparing for the challenges. “During the Osun State election, for instance, we engaged corps members, their parents and other stakeholders and assured them of our commitment to providing adequate security for all ad hoc personnel. We came out unscathed. The forthcoming general election will not be an exception,” he said. The police spokesman said the force was working with sister security agencies and engaging INEC to strengthen protection for corps members and other personnel involved in the electoral process. He added that deployments were being increased, while the Inspector-General of Police had directed the immediate distribution of operational equipment and logistics. Emphasising that the safety of corps members and other young Nigerians participating in the electoral process remained a priority, Iniedu said the police would do everything within their capacity to protect them. He also warned political actors against hate speech, incitement and other forms of political violence capable of undermining the electoral process. According to him, the police have documented 11 reported cases of hate speech and taken action in response to them. “Hate speech and incitement are criminal offences. The Inspector-General of Police has directed all Commissioners of Police to ensure the immediate arrest and prosecution of individuals involved in such acts,” he said. Iniedu added that the police had established complaint channels through which members of the public could report commissioners who failed to take appropriate action against offenders. “We will be taking decisive action against offenders. item.title: Shettima rally: SDP denies sponsoring disruption, faults Nasarawa govt
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Nasarawa State has denied allegations linking its governorship candidate, retired Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, and former Governor Tanko Al-Makura to the disruption of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Lafia. The party also accused the Nasarawa State Government of attempting to find scapegoats among opposition figures following the incident at Lafia Square on Wednesday, where President Bola Tinubu was represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima. Reacting to the allegation in a statement on Thursday, Deputy Director-General, Media, Publicity and Communication, and spokesperson for the SDP governorship campaign council, Makpa Malla, described a statement by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Shuaibu Magaji Labaran, as reckless, irresponsible and politically motivated. Malla particularly faulted the government’s reference to Al-Makura and Adamu as suspected sponsors of the disruption, describing it as a serious allegation of criminal complicity and conspiracy. “The most disturbing aspect of the government’s statement is paragraph three, which expressly names H.E. Senator Umaru Tanko Al-Makura and rtd. IGP Mohammed Abubakar Adamu, the Governorship Candidate of the SDP, as suspected sponsors of the alleged disruption,” the statement said. The campaign council argued that publicly linking the individuals to an alleged criminal act without presenting verifiable evidence raised questions about defamation, due process and the alleged abuse of governmental authority. It maintained that the use of the expression “suspected to be sponsored” did not absolve the government of responsibility for making damaging allegations against identifiable individuals. The SDP said if the government had credible intelligence implicating the individuals, it should submit such evidence to the appropriate investigative authorities rather than make public accusations. It cautioned against what it described as a trial by press release, insisting that political opponents should not be pronounced guilty in the court of public opinion. The party also criticised the state government over what it described as more pressing governance challenges, including political grievances arising from the APC’s internal primaries, which it claimed contributed to tensions surrounding the incident. The SDP, however, said it would welcome the outcome of an independent, evidence-based investigation into the disruption, provided it was free from political interference. It specifically called for the Department of State Services (DSS), which is expected to investigate the incident, to be allowed to discharge its responsibilities professionally without pressure to validate predetermined allegations. “The DSS must be allowed to do its work professionally, without being turned into an instrument for settling political scores or intimidating perceived political opponents,” the

item.title: France Workers Strike, March For ‘Dignified Wage’
item.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. More than 250,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across 73 cities by the afternoon, the major labour union CGT said. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. Protesters take part in a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Bordeaux on November 5, 2026. Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP Protesting in the city of Lyon, winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations he saw as drawing together people from across French society. “We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage,” he said. As many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2:00 pm (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. The planned action prompted the Eiffel Tower to close for the day, operators said on the monument’s website. School blockades Dozens of high-schoolers protested in several cities, with the government reporting blockades at 81 out of the country’s 3,700 high schools. A high school student association said classes had been suspended at 1,000 such secondary schools, including those blockaded and those closed on a day of strikes. Around 16 percent of teachers nationwide were on strike, the education ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas to try to prevent students from blocking access to the Helene-Boucher high school, an AFP reporter said. French police officers march amid the smoke during a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks, in Nantes on November 5, 2026. item.title: ‘Why We Should Continue To Support Tinubu’, Wike To Nigerians
item.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, has explained the many reasons Nigerians should re-elect President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. The FCT Minister spoke on Wednesday during his monthly ministerial press briefing in Port Harcourt on Thursday. Wike said he enjoyed his job as FCT Minister and remained committed to it. “I enjoy my job as FCT Minister, and I’m committed to it. Yes, I have pressure to deliver, but positively,” he said. Wike also said Ogoni people had benefited from empowerment under the President. “Ogoni people have been looking for empowerment, and now President Tinubu has done a lot of empowerment for them. If you tell them not to vote for Mr President, they’ll look at you like you’re not okay,” he said. He insisted that “no government has done more in the fight against insecurity than this government.” The former Rivers State governor responded to critics and political rivals, including the Turaki-led PDP faction, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodinma, and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), University of Abuja branch.
